bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Drinking Water Project Wins Rs 1,774 Crore NABARD Backing Breaking News Bihar Drinking Water Project Wins Rs 1,774 Crore NABARD Backing By Maria Dsouza October 30, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has announced a Rs 2,014 crore drinking water project for Aurangabad, Sasaram and Dehri, with Rs 1,774 crore approved by NABARD to upgrade water infrastructure under the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund. The scheme will use surface water from the Sone river to strengthen existing supply systems in the three towns. The announcement was made by the chief minister on Thursday, according to a statement from the Chief Minister’s Office. Choudhary said the project would expand drinking water facilities and improve water availability in the three areas. The state government said the scheme would initially serve a population of around 8 lakh. The project is expected to cover nearly 12 lakh people by 2051, indicating that the planned infrastructure is being designed around long-term population growth in the three towns. The announcement did not provide details of the proposed treatment capacity, distribution network, construction schedule, tendering process or commissioning date. The funding approved by NABARD is part of the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund, which supports infrastructure projects through institutional financing. The statement did not specify how the remaining amount from the total project cost would be financed or provide a town-wise allocation for Aurangabad, Sasaram and Dehri. The proposed use of Sone river water will reinforce existing drinking water systems rather than replace them, according to the chief minister’s statement. The announcement therefore links the project to both source augmentation and the strengthening of civic supply infrastructure. Details on water treatment facilities, transmission lines, storage arrangements and household-level connections were not included in the information released. Choudhary also linked the initiative to Bihar’s Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali campaign, which promotes water conservation, environmental protection and the sustainable use of water resources. The project’s stated objective is to provide residents with clean and adequate drinking water while expanding the capacity of urban and surrounding supply systems. The announcement places the three towns within a wider state effort to improve basic infrastructure with support from the Union government and financial institutions. For residents, the eventual impact will depend on how quickly the approved funding is converted into construction, treatment and distribution capacity, as well as how the expanded network is operated and maintained. The Bihar government has not yet announced the project’s implementation timeline, construction milestones or completion date. Further details are expected as the scheme moves from funding approval to execution. The project is expected to serve around 8 lakh people initially and nearly 12 lakh by 2051. The Chief Minister’s Office said on Thursday that NABARD had approved Rs 1,774 crore for upgrading Bihar’s drinking water infrastructure under the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF). The remaining components of the Rs 2,014 crore investment were not detailed in the statement. The project will draw surface water from the Sone river to reinforce existing drinking water systems in Aurangabad, Sasaram and Dehri. The announcement did not specify the planned treatment capacity, distribution network length, construction schedule or the individual allocation for each town. Choudhary thanked Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the Union government for supporting the project through the financing approval. According to the statement, the state government considers the scheme part of its broader effort to expand basic infrastructure and improve civic amenities across Bihar. The proposed coverage numbers indicate that the scheme has been planned around both current demand and long-term population growth. The three towns together are expected to see the number of people covered rise from approximately 8 lakh at present to nearly 12 lakh by 2051. The statement did not provide a projected date for commissioning the system or details of the phases in which the network will be developed. The use of Sone river water will add a surface-water source to the towns’ existing supply arrangements. The announcement described the project as a measure to improve water availability, but did not set out the present reliability of supplies, the condition of existing infrastructure or the treatment and transmission systems that will be upgraded. The Chief Minister also linked the initiative to the Jal-Jeevan-Hariyali campaign, which focuses on water conservation, environmental protection and the sustainable use of water resources. The statement presented the drinking water project as part of that wider approach to managing water and expanding access to basic services. NABARD’s approval under RIDF provides the principal financing commitment disclosed so far. The Rural Infrastructure Development Fund is being used in this case to support drinking water infrastructure, while implementation will be undertaken by the Bihar government. The supplied announcement did not identify the executing agency, procurement process, land requirements or safeguards connected with drawing water from the Sone. The state government said it remained committed to ensuring that residents had access to clean and adequate drinking water. The next publicly stated step is the implementation of the approved project, although the announcement did not provide a tender deadline, construction timetable or commissioning milestone. national_raw_news.title: World Stroke Day: Nadda Urges Citizens to Recognise Stroke Warning Signs
national_raw_news.content: World Stroke Day is being observed today to raise awareness about stroke and the importance of recognising its warning signs. This year’s campaign message, ‘Every Minute Counts – Know the Signs of Stroke’, reminds everyone that timely action can save lives. On the occasion, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Jagat Prakash Nadda said, sudden facial drooping, weakness in an arm, or difficulty speaking should never be ignored. He emphasised that seeking immediate medical attention can make a crucial difference in recovery. He urged citizens to learn the warning signs, spread awareness, and encourage everyone to act quickly, as every minute matters. Talking to Akashvani News, Chief of the Neurosciences Centre at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, Dr Shailesh B Gaikwad said, stroke is a serious neurological emergency in which the blood supply to part of the brain is interrupted or a blood vessel in the brain ruptures. He said, with around 18 lakh stroke cases recorded across India each year, awareness can save lives. He added that the symptoms of the stroke include sudden loss or blurring of vision, double vision, loss of balance, and difficulty in walking. Dr Gaikwad emphasized if such symptoms are visible then the patients should immediately transfer to stroke ready hospital for treatment. Dr Gaikwad further added that high blood pressure is one of the leading risk factors for stroke. He added that other factors include diabetes, high cholesterol, certain heart conditions, smoking, excessive alcohol consumption, obesity, physical inactivity, and an unhealthy diet. Dr gaikwad informed that the risk increases with age, but stroke can occur at any age. He advised regular health check-ups and proper control of these risk factors.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi to Launch Projects Worth ₹14,000 Crore in Gujarat
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will be on a two-day visit to Gujarat, beginning tomorrow. Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over 14 thousand crore rupees in Banaskantha tomorrow. The Prime Minister will lay the foundation stone of Ahmedabad Metro Phase-2A (Airport Extension) and Phase-2B (GIFT City Extension). He will also release the 24th instalment under PM-KISAN, amounting to 19 thousand crore rupees. He will also visit the Embryo Transfer Technology-In Vitro Fertilisation Laboratory and the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre cattle farm in Banaskantha. The Centre will strengthen bovine breeding, genetic upgradation and advanced reproductive technologies, accelerating breed improvement by 10 to 20 times. Thereafter, the Prime Minister will travel to Ekta Nagar, Kevadia and inaugurate Bharat Parv 2026. On Saturday, Prime Minister Modi will offer floral tributes at the Statue of Unity. Mr Modi will lay the foundation stone, inaugurate and dedicate to the nation various development projects worth over four hundred crore rupees in Ekta Nagar. The projects include a sewage and water treatment plant, facade lighting, the upgradation of Narmada Ghat, and the Rainforest, among others. The Prime Minister will also participate in the Rashtriya Ekta Diwas celebrations commemorating the 151st birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

national_raw_news.title: Sports, Education Ministries and UNESCO sign MoU to take clean sport values to every classroom 28 Oct 2026 | 8:08 PM 189
national_raw_news.content: The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Ministry of Education and UNESCO today exchanged a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to take clean sport values to classrooms across India through the ‘Sports Values in Every Classroom Toolkit’. The MoU was exchanged in the presence of Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya, Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi, Director of UNESCO’s Regional Office for South Asia, Dr Tim Curtis. Addressing the event, Mr joshi said that the MoU would help address the longstanding gap between education and sports. He also said that students who performed well academically did not always participate in sports, and emphasised the need to strengthen grassroots opportunities and build better pathways for young athletes. Meanwhile, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr Mansukh Mandaviya said that sporting excellence and sporting integrity must go hand in hand. He added that talent, discipline and hard work are essential for sporting success, but integrity, fairness and credibility are equally important. The initiative is aimed at embedding values such as respect, integrity and fairness in children through education, sports and everyday classroom activities. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said that the toolkit’s video modules will be made available in 13 Indian languages, with the objective of reaching students across the country and building a stronger, fairer sporting ecosystem.

national_raw_news.title: Union Cabinet approves 3% hike in Dearness Allowance for central government employees
national_raw_news.content: The Union Cabinet has approved the Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme to promote domestic manufacturing.The total outlay for the scheme is ten thousand crore rupees for 13 years upto Financial Year 2039-40. The scheme aims to establish a globally competitive container manufacturing ecosystem in India, reduce import dependence and strengthen supply chain resilience. Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that the scheme is intended to support new manufacturing facilities as well as expansion of existing container manufacturing units. He said, it has four components including Interest Subvention Assistance, Testing and Certification assistance, Land Leasing support and Operational Expenditure Assistance. Mr Vaishnaw added that the scheme will create an internationally competitive manufacturing base, with potential to position India as a global export hub for quality shipping containers. The Container Manufacturing Promotion Scheme will strengthen resilience of India’s maritime and logistics supply chains. It will generate an estimated 3,000 direct jobs and over 50,000 indirect jobs, while supporting ancillary industries such as corner castings, specialised steel, wooden frames and paints. Mr Vaishnaw informed that Union Cabinet also approved three percent increase in Dearness Allowance to Central Government employees and Dearness Relief to Pensioners with effect from 1st of July,2026. Mr Vaishnaw added that this will benefit over 48 lakh Central Government employees and 68 lakh pensioners. The Union Cabinet has also approved the Khelo India Sports Goods Manufacturing Scheme to position India as a global hub for high-quality sports goods. Giving details about the scheme , Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said that that the scheme has an approved outlay of over one thousand 856 crore rupees over eight years period from 2026-27 to 2033-34. He said, the scheme will support the development of a globally competitive sports goods industry and strengthen India’s position in global supply chains. Mr Vaishnaw said that the Scheme envisages the development of dedicated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones (SGMZs) to promote cluster-based manufacturing and create integrated industrial ecosystems. Mr Vaishnaw added that incentives and interventions are the two parts of the scheme where incentive supports manufacturing while intervetion builds the wider ecosystem. The Union Minister also said that a key focus of the Scheme is to attract new investments and strengthen domestic manufacturing capacity in the sports goods sector. The Anchor Investment Support component will encourage leading domestic and global manufacturers, brands and retail chains to establish manufacturing facilities within designated Sports Goods Manufacturing Zones and foster the development of robust supplier and ancillary ecosystems. Complementing this, the Turnover Linked Support component will incentivise higher production, capacity expansion and sustained manufacturing growth. Mr Vaishnaw also informed that the Union Cabinet has approved the Pradhan Mantri Viksit Gram Swaraj Yojana (PMVGSY) scheme as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme. It aims to transform Panchayats into empowered, self-reliant, accountable and high-performing institutions of local self-government, in line with the vision of Viksit Bharat. Mr Vaishnaw said that the scheme has a total financial outlay of 7,395 crore rupees and the duration of the scheme is for five years from 2026-27 to 2030-31. He said, the scheme applies to all States and Union Territories, including rural local governance institutions in non-Part IX areas where Panchayats do not exist. It will cover more than 2.78 lakh Rural Local Bodies and Traditional Bodies across the country. Mr Vaishnaw said, around 32 lakh elected representatives, along with Panchayat functionaries and other stakeholders, across over 2.55 lakh Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies will be direct beneficiaries of the scheme. The combined impact on the exchequer on account of increase in both Dearness Allowance and Dearness Relief would be over 10,000 crore rupees per annum.

national_raw_news.title: Cyclone Arnab damages over 80,000 hectares of crops in Andhra Pradesh
national_raw_news.content: Cyclone Arnab has caused extensive damage to crops, houses, roads and power infrastructure across several districts of Andhra Pradesh. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has requested the Centre to send an inter-ministerial team for an early assessment of the losses. The State Government has intensified relief and restoration operations in the affected areas. Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewed cyclone relief operations through the State’s Real-Time Governance Centre and directed officials to expedite restoration of essential services. The Chief Minister announced an ex-gratia of five lakh rupees each to the families of those who lost their lives and financial assistance to affected households. Preliminary estimates indicate damage to over 70 thousand hectares of paddy and more than 10 thousand hectares of horticultural crops. Over 28 thousand people have been evacuated to relief shelters, with NDRF and SDRF teams deployed across affected districts. Electricity restoration is progressing, with nearly 80 percent of power supply restored in Visakhapatnam district. Repair work is continuing in Konaseema, Kakinada and the Godavari districts, where fallen trees and damaged electricity poles disrupted services. Officials are also clearing blocked roads and restoring drinking water supplies. Meanwhile, the Chief Minister has requested Centre to send a team to assess cyclone-related losses.

national_raw_news.title: US Federal Reserve keeps its key interest rate unchanged at 3.9% despite high inflation
national_raw_news.content: The US Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged at a target range of 3.75 per cent to 4.00 per cent, keeping the average effective rate at approximately 3.9 per cent despite stubbornly high inflation. In a statement released after its two-day policy meeting, the Fed said, inflation remains elevated and holding off on an increase will allow the accumulation of more information that will help determine what policy the Fed should pursue to ensure a timely return of inflation to the central bank’s 2 per cent target. The statement leaves the Fed’s next moves unclear, even though officials last month pencilled in another rate hike for this year. The Fed’s decision comes just six days before a midterm election that has focused heavily on concerns around the cost of living and affordability. Two Fed officials dissented from yesterday’s decision, with Fed governor Lisa Cook and Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack voting in favour of hiking rates by a quarter point. Consumers have generally soured on an economy weighed down by more expensive gas, groceries, and clothing, among other items. Yet Warsh faces plenty of challenges in getting inflation back to target. Other parts of the economy are already being hit by higher rates, which were lifted by market forces, even before the Fed hiked last month. Inflation picked up in September, when consumer prices rose 3.7 per cent compared with a year earlier. The increase was much bigger than the 2.4 per cent rate in February, just before the Iran war. The Fed, led by Chairman Kevin Warsh, raised its benchmark rate last month for the first time in three years, defying President Donald Trump’s demands for rate cuts. President Trump has also slammed the Fed for raising its key rate last month, though he largely blamed the central bank’s rate-setting committee, rather than Warsh, whom he appointed. Many economists argue that solid growth is evidence that interest rates aren’t particularly high and the economy could withstand higher rates to combat inflation.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the 54th meeting of PRAGATI, the ICT-enabled, multi-modal platform aimed at fostering Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation, at Seva Teerth in New Delhi yesterday. During the meeting, the Prime Minister reviewed infrastructure projects across the Railways, Ekta Malls and Drug Parks worth over 16 thousand crore rupees covering 31 States and Union Territories. Pivotal to economic growth and public welfare, these projects, were reviewed with a focus on timeliness, inter-agency coordination, and timely issue resolution. Prime Minister asked the concerned Ministries and State Governments to resolve bottlenecks in mission mode, strengthen Centre-State and inter-agency coordination, and ensure close monitoring at the senior-most level. Calling for a proactive work culture with greater ownership at every level, he stressed the need to anticipate implementation challenges, take timely decisions and fix clear accountability for completing projects on schedule. Prime Minister Modi also asked Chief Secretaries to review schemes with District Magistrates every month to address implementation gaps and ensure that benefits reach eligible beneficiaries on time. He emphasised that governance must focus on outcomes over outlays, ensuring that public expenditure translates into tangible improvements in people’s lives. Prime Minister Modi stressed that PM Ekta Malls should provide markets for local products, strengthen the livelihoods of artisans and help them expand their enterprises. He emphasised the need for regular review of progress by Chief Secretaries and to ensure timely completion of the malls. Reviewing Bulk Drug Parks in Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Himachal Pradesh, Mr Modi stressed the need to prioritise domestic production of active pharmaceutical ingredients and essential inputs to strengthen self-reliance. Referring to the Aspirational Districts and Aspirational Blocks Programmes, Mr Modi highlighted the role of convergence, regular monitoring and local accountability in accelerating development in underserved areas. He noted that sustained efforts to strengthen governance and improve the delivery of welfare schemes had helped nearly 25 crore people move out of multidimensional poverty. During the review of the redevelopment of Ahmedabad railway station, Mr Modi called for expediting the redevelopment of major railway stations across the country to improve passenger convenience and ease of travel. He emphasised that redeveloped stations should serve as multimodal transport hubs, with seamless connectivity to metro and other transport networks.

Excelsior Correspondent JAMMU, Oct 28: A one-day workshop on vigilance awareness for employees of CBC and the Press Information Bureau (PIB) organized by the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC) was held here today. The workshop was organized on the theme "Probity for Prosperity", emphasizing the importance of integrity, transparency and accountability in public administration. Speaking on the occasion, Director, CBC/PIB Jammu, Neha Jalali highlighted the importance of honesty, transparency and accountability in the discharge of official duties. She stressed that integrity and ethical conduct must be reflected in day-to-day official dealings and that public servants should perform their responsibilities with a strong sense of duty, fairness and commitment to public service. Deputy Superintendent, Anti-Corruption Bureau, Kamal Sangra raised awareness about various aspects of corruption, its adverse impact on public administration and the importance of vigilance in preventing corrupt practices. He also explained the circumstances and considerations that led to the introduction of the Public Interest Disclosure and Protection of Informers (PIDPI) Resolution, which provides a mechanism for reporting allegations of corruption and protecting the identity of persons making such disclosures, subject to the prescribed procedure. The participants were briefed on the scope and applicability of the resolution, including the distinction between its applicability to Central Government employees and its non-applicability to State Government employees under the framework discussed. Senior Accounts Officer CBC, Rajesh Malik; Administrative Officer, O P Maurya; Media and Communication Officer PIB, Muzafar Wani and other employees of CBC and PIB Jammu attended the workshop. national_raw_news.title: Special Campaign 6.0: Pharmaceuticals Department conducts 14,700 cleanliness drives ...
national_raw_news.content: Special Campaign 6.0: Pharmaceuticals Department conducts 14,700 cleanliness drives, generates ₹2.30 lakh from scrap disposal Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Special Campaign 6.0: Pharmaceuticals Department conducts 14,700 cleanliness drives, generates ₹2.30 lakh from scrap disposal ANI | Updated: Oct 29, 2026 01:07 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 29 (ANI): The Department of Pharmaceuticals , under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilisers, along with its attached office, the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority, and associated organisations including seven NIPERs, the PMBI, and three public sector undertakings namely BCPL, HAL, and KAPL, is actively participating in the Special Campaign for Disposal of Pending Matters 6.0. Being conducted from October 2 to October 31, the campaign focuses on promoting cleanliness, scientific management and disposal of e-waste, systematic record management, effective grievance redressal, and optimum utilisation of office space, to enhance administrative efficiency and promote a clean, organised, and productive work environment. Across field and outstation offices, 14,700 cleanliness drives have been conducted so far against a baseline target of 12,208, reflecting the Department’s continued efforts to improve workplace hygiene and sanitation, strengthen environmental awareness, and foster sustainable workplace practices, an official release stated. The campaign has strengthened systematic record management and promoted the efficient utilisation of office space. Against a baseline target of 2,716 physical files and 20 e-files, the Department has reviewed 4,283 physical files and 20 e-files, while 489 files have been weeded out and closed. Additionally, 2,200 square feet of office space has been freed up through these efforts, contributing to better space management and the creation of more organised, efficient, and clutter-free workplaces. Administrative efficiency and responsive governance are being strengthened through the timely resolution of pending matters, including MP references (3 against a target of 4), parliamentary assurances(1 out of 2), a Cabinet proposal (02 proposals), State references (57 against 58) and PMO references (02 cases). Against the target of 72 public grievances and 28 appeals registered on the Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS), 132 public grievance cases and 39 appeals have been settled. Against a target of 20 items identified for easing of rules/processes, this has been completed for 17 items. These efforts aim to expedite the resolution of pending matters, improve service delivery, and promote greater accountability and efficiency in public administration. The Ministry of Chemicals also mentioned that scientific e-waste management is one of the key focus areas of SCDPM 6. The Department has targeted 1,011 obsolete electronic and electrical items - comprising IT equipment, consumer electronics, appliances, and laboratory tools - for safe disposal through empanelled recyclers under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022. The process for disposing of these items is currently underway. Further, the Department has earned revenue of Rs 2,30,187/- from the disposal of office scrap. Department of Pharmaceuticals remains committed to the objectives of SCDPM 6 and is monitoring targets closely and documenting achievements via the National Special Campaign Portal, the release stated. AI Quick Read The Union Cabinet has approved a 3-percentage-point increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) for central government employees and Dearness Relief (DR) for pensioners, Union Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced on 28 October 2026. The decision will benefit around 48.54 lakh central government employees and 68.71 lakh pensioners. Calling the increase a Diwali gift from Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Vaishnaw said the Cabinet had approved the revision at its meeting on Wednesday. According to the Press Information Bureau (PIB), the revised rates will be effective from 1 July 2026. The hike takes DA and DR from 60% to 63% of basic pay and pension, respectively. The combined annual impact on the government exchequer is estimated at ₹ 10,016.10 crore, according to the official announcement. The increase follows the accepted formula based on the recommendations of the 7th Central Pay Commission. How much will central government employees gain from the 3% DA hike? The additional amount employees receive will depend on their basic pay. A 3-percentage-point increase in DA translates into an additional 3% of basic pay every month. For instance, an employee drawing basic pay of ₹ 18,000 will receive an additional ₹ 540 per month. For an employee with basic pay of ₹ 25,000, the monthly increase will be ₹ 750. Someone with basic pay of ₹ 50,000 will receive an additional ₹ 1,500 per month. Adhil Shetty, CEO of BankBazaar, said the increase follows the established formula linked to inflation data under the 7th Pay Commission. “At Level 3 and Level 8, basic pay of ₹ 21,700 and ₹ 47,600 respectively, the increase adds ₹ 651 and ₹ 1,428 a month, with arrears due separately,” Shetty said. He added that employees could use the additional income to strengthen their savings rather than absorb it into everyday spending. “What matters next is where that money goes. Channeled into a recurring deposit, an SIP, or an emergency fund rather than daily spending, even a modest hike can gradually build into meaningful savings over time,” he said. DA is intended to help government employees offset the impact of inflation on household expenses. The Centre typically revises the allowance twice a year, with changes effective from January and July. How much more pension will retirees receive after the DR hike? national_raw_news.title: Union Health Minister JP Nadda reviews cleanliness initiatives under Special Campaign 6 at AIIMS
national_raw_news.content: Union Health Minister JP Nadda reviews cleanliness initiatives under Special Campaign 6 at AIIMS Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Health Minister JP Nadda reviews cleanliness initiatives under Special Campaign 6 at AIIMS ANI | Updated: Oct 29, 2026 18:41 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 29 (ANI): Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare JP Nadda visited the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi , on Thursday to review cleanliness, sanitation and waste management initiatives undertaken by the institute under Special Campaign 6 . According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, during the visit, he also inspected the newly constructed Patient Waiting Lounge at the AIIMS Trauma Centre Extension Campus, developed by Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL), Ghaziabad, under its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) initiative and proposed to be utilised as an Aashray Shelter for patients and their attendants. He also interacted with sanitation workers at the institute. The Union Health Minister was briefed on the initiatives undertaken by AIIMS under the Swachhata Abhiyan, with particular focus on cleanliness, sanitation, waste management and the upkeep of institutional premises. AIIMS, New Delhi , has adopted several best practices to strengthen sanitation and hygiene, including gang washing, dedicated sanitary attendants in emergency and OPD toilets, end-of-day OPD cleaning, regular training of sanitation workers, timely wage payments and monitoring of sanitation supplies and mechanised cleaning equipment. The institute has also undertaken significant measures in water and energy conservation. Its 11 wastewater treatment plants are supported by online monitoring and smart metering, with approximately 19.6 lakh litres of treated wastewater reused daily for horticulture. Energy conservation measures, including optimised air-conditioning and switching off equipment when not required, have resulted in a reported reduction of 7.68 lakh kWh in electricity consumption, a decline of 10.5 per cent. Electricity expenditure was about Rs 1.98 crore lower during January–October 2025 compared with the corresponding period in 2024. To promote sustainable mobility, AIIMS operates 40 free in-campus electric vehicle shuttle services for patients and attendants. The campus also has 30 EV chargers and 114 dedicated power points across four locations, supported by smart monitoring systems, the release stated. These initiatives reflect AIIMS’ commitment to institutionalising cleanliness, improving resource efficiency and maintaining a hygienic, sustainable and patient-friendly healthcare environment under Special Campaign 6 . Following the briefing, Nadda proceeded to the newly constructed Patient Waiting Lounge at the AIIMS Trauma Centre Extension Campus to inspect the infrastructure and facilities developed for patients and their attendants. Constructed by BEL, Ghaziabad, under its CSR initiative, the facility has a revised built-up area of 2,970 square metres and a designed seating capacity of 897 persons. The building comprises primary and secondary waiting areas, entry and exit points, ramps, toilets and ancillary facilities. The completed facility is proposed to be utilised as an Aashray Shelter to provide safe, dignified and weather-protected temporary accommodation for economically disadvantaged patients and their attendants who travel to AIIMS for medical treatment. national_raw_news.content: INS Trishul concludes port call in Italy as Indian Navy strengthens maritime cooperation with Italian counterpart Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर INS Trishul concludes port call in Italy as Indian Navy strengthens maritime cooperation with Italian counterpart ANI | Updated: Oct 29, 2026 19:05 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel Civitavecchia [ Italy ], October 29 (ANI): India n Naval Ship Trishul concluded its port call at Civitavecchia, Italy , as part of its ongoing operational deployment in the Mediterranean Sea, with engagements aimed at strengthening maritime cooperation and professional ties between the India n Navy and the Italian Navy. According to the press release, the port call concluded on Wednesday with professional interactions, cross-deck visits and cultural exchanges, providing opportunities for personnel from both navies to interact and exchange experiences. During the visit, the Commanding Officer of INS Trishul called on the Fleet Commander of the Italian Navy. The ship's crew also visited the Italian Navy's aircraft carrier ITS Cavour at Civitavecchia as part of the professional engagements. The interactions provided an opportunity for personnel from the two navies to share professional experiences and further their understanding of each other's operational practices. INS Trishul was also open to visitors during its stay, attracting a large number of members of the India n diaspora and the local population. India 's Ambassador to Italy , Vani Rao, and Vice Admiral Aurelio De Carolis, Fleet Commander and CINCNAV of the Italian Navy, visited INS Trishul and interacted with the ship's crew. According to the release, both dignitaries also attended a cultural event hosted onboard the India n naval vessel. The event brought together the Mayor of Civitavecchia, senior officers of the Italian Navy and Coast Guard, Defence Envoys from 13 nations, civil dignitaries and members of the India n diaspora. The gathering provided a platform for interaction among naval representatives, diplomatic officials and members of the wider community, complementing the professional engagements undertaken during the port call. Following the conclusion of its port call, INS Trishul proceeded to the next phase of its operational deployment in the Mediterranean Sea. national_raw_news.title: Union Minister of Jal Shakti C R Patil chairs 19th meeting of Ganga Flood Control Board in New Delhi
national_raw_news.content: Union Minister of Jal Shakti C R Patil chairs 19th meeting of Ganga Flood Control Board in New Delhi Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर Union Minister of Jal Shakti C R Patil chairs 19th meeting of Ganga Flood Control Board in New Delhi ANI | Updated: Oct 29, 2026 14:51 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 29 (ANI): The 19th Meeting of the Ganga Flood Control Board (GFCB) was held at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on Thursday under the chairmanship of Union Minister of Jal Shakti, C R Patil. The meeting was also attended by West Bengal Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari. According to the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti, the meeting reviewed ongoing initiatives, strengthened interstate coordination and deliberated on emerging approaches for effective flood management. During the meeting, the Jal Shakti Minister launched the Punah Bharan Mobile App, developed by the Bhaskaracharya National Institute for Space Applications and Geo-informatics in collaboration with the National Water Mission. The application aims to facilitate scientific identification of suitable locations for artificial groundwater recharge interventions. The Board deliberated on the revised mandate and restructuring of the Ganga Flood Control Commission (GFCC), which includes strengthening basin-level flood management planning, appraisal of flood management schemes, river morphology and sedimentation studies, and development of a Flood Management Information System (FMIS). The revised institutional arrangements are expected to improve coordination, technical appraisal and timely decision-making. The discussions also focused on preparation of risk-based basin Master Plans, assessment of the adequacy of waterways and ventways under bridges, improving the quality of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs), timely implementation of flood management projects and application of modern technologies in flood management, the Ministry stated. Emphasis was laid on strengthening coordination among Central Ministries, State Governments and other stakeholders, particularly in addressing issues relating to river morphology, drainage congestion, infrastructure development and flood resilience. The importance of modern survey techniques, sound technical investigations, appropriate statutory clearances and timely resolution of project implementation bottlenecks was also highlighted. The meeting reaffirmed the importance of an integrated, risk-informed and technology-enabled approach to flood management, supported by effective Centre–State cooperation, improved technical standards and coordinated implementation of flood management measures across the Ganga Basin. The Ganga Flood Control Board (GFCB) was constituted by the Government of India on 18 April 1972 to facilitate coordinated planning and implementation of measures to address flood, erosion and drainage problems in the Ganga Basin, the Ministry stated. The Board is chaired by the Union Minister of Jal Shakti and comprises representatives of the concerned Central Ministries and Chief Ministers of the Ganga Basin States or their representatives, with the Chairman, GFCC, serving as its Member Secretary. It provides a high-level institutional platform for strengthening Centre–State cooperation and coordinated flood management across the Ganga Basin. national_raw_news.title: 14th International Tourism Mart inaugurated in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang - ANI News
national_raw_news.content: 14th International Tourism Mart inaugurated in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang Toggle navigation हिंदी खबर 14th International Tourism Mart inaugurated in Arunachal Pradesh's Tawang ANI | Updated: Oct 30, 2026 03:59 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 30 (ANI): The 14th edition of the International Tourism Mart (ITM), organised by the Ministry of Tourism, Government of India, in association with the Government of Arunachal Pradesh and other North Eastern States, commenced on Thursday at Tawang , Arunachal Pradesh . The three-day Mart, being held from October 29 to 31, aims to showcase the tourism potential of the eight North Eastern States and strengthen business engagement with domestic and international tourism markets. The inaugural session was held in the presence of Gajendra Singh Shekhawat , Union Minister for Tourism and Culture; Suresh Gopi, Union Minister of State for Tourism and Petroleum & Natural Gas; Sukanta Majumdar, Union Minister of State for Education and Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER); Pema Khandu, Chief Minister of Arunachal Pradesh ; and Prem Singh Tamang, Chief Minister of Sikkim. Tourism Ministers from the North Eastern States, senior officials of the Central and State Governments, international and domestic tourism stakeholders and representatives of the travel industry were also present. Addressing the inaugural session, Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat emphasised that the International Tourism Mart has evolved beyond a promotional platform into an important avenue for tourism partnerships and business opportunities. He stated, “ITM is not merely a tourism marketplace; it is a platform for building partnerships, generating business opportunities and creating a shared vision for the growth of tourism in the North East Region.” Highlighting the immense potential of the region, the Minister said that its rich biodiversity, cultural heritage, spiritual traditions and natural landscapes offer distinctive opportunities for adventure, nature-based and experiential tourism. He particularly emphasised the potential of adventure tourism, music festivals and concert tourism to attract new visitor segments, encourage longer stays and generate economic opportunities for local communities. He also called for developing tourism experiences with appropriate safety standards, community participation and environmental safeguards. The Minister highlighted the Government’s continued focus on improving connectivity, tourism infrastructure and destination experiences in the North Eastern Region. He also underlined the Ministry’s support for tourism promotion through domestic and international travel fairs, festivals, digital platforms and familiarisation visits, along with skill development initiatives to create employment opportunities for local youth. national_raw_news.content: India Post, UTI Mutual Fund extend partnership for doorstep KYC verification across India | Business About Career Advertisement Media Partnership Contact Us HOME NEWS RESEARCH LIVE DISCOURSE PERSPECTIVES AND INSIGHTS SUBMIT PRESS RELEASE NEWS DESK RESEARCH LIVE DISCOURSE PERSPECTIVES AND INSIGHTS INTERVIEW Home News Law & Governance Article India Post, UTI Mutual Fund extend partnership for doorstep KYC verification across India India Post and UTI Mutual Fund have extended their existing partnership to expand doorstep Know Your Customer (KYC) verification services for mutual fund investors across India, particularly in remote and underserved areas. ANI | Updated: 29-10-2026 21:10 IST | Created: 29-10-2026 21:10 IST Senior officials from the Department of Posts and UTI AMC during the meeting at UTI AMC’s Corporate Office (Photo/PIB). Image Credit: ANI SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... India Post and UTI Mutual Fund have extended their existing partnership to expand doorstep Know Your Customer (KYC) verification services for mutual fund investors across India, particularly in remote and underserved areas. According to a release issued by the Ministry of Communications on Thursday, the expanded collaboration aims to simplify investor verification, improve access to mutual fund services and strengthen financial inclusion. "Under the Pan-India KYC Verification Project, India Post will leverage its extensive postal network and last-mile connectivity to facilitate Know Your Customer (KYC) verification at investors' doorsteps, including in remote and underserved areas," the ministry said. The Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) extending the existing agreement was signed by Adnan Ahmed, Chief General Manager, Parcel & CCS Directorate, Department of Posts, and Vetri Subramaniam, Managing Director and CEO of UTI Asset Management Company Limited, in Mumbai on Thursday. The expanded partnership builds on an earlier KYC remediation initiative that helped investors complete pending verification requirements and address documentation gaps. "Building on the earlier KYC remediation initiative, which helped investors complete pending KYC requirements, improve compliance and address documentation gaps, the expanded collaboration is expected to strengthen investor servicing, encourage wider participation in mutual funds and support uninterrupted access to mutual fund investments," the release stated. India Post has already been providing doorstep KYC verification services for mutual fund investors. According to an earlier Ministry of Communications release issued in April 2025, India Post had completed over 5 lakh KYC verifications for UTI and the Specified Undertaking of the Unit Trust of India (SUUTI). The Department of Posts subsequently signed similar agreements with Nippon India Mutual Fund in April 2025 and SBI Mutual Fund later that month. In July 2025, India Post also entered into an agreement with the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) to facilitate KYC verification for mutual fund investors through its network of over 1.64 lakh post offices.
